subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice-pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow early feedback, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but the requested fix crosses Telegram ingress ordering, audio preflight authorization, STT/TTS provider behavior, reply delivery semantics, caching policy, and session-state visibility, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Stage a measured async pipeline
options.body: Keep this as the broad tracker, use narrower issues for typing cues and delivery modes, and design async STT/TTS with ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks before coding.

options.title: Limit scope to feedback and delivery
options.body: Treat immediate typing cues and a text/voice delivery policy as the near-term fixes while leaving deeper priority queues, streaming, and caching unplanned.

options.title: Defer broad pipeline work
options.body: Keep current provider tuning and delivery semantics until live evidence shows a staged voice pipeline is worth the added complexity.

recommendation.title: Stage a measured async pipeline
recommendation.body: Keep this as the broad tracker, use narrower issues for typing cues and delivery modes, and design async STT/TTS with ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined history across Telegram audio preflight, TTS core, and reply/inbound queue behavior.
